# Results — Study 783 (IPO-Deal-Of-Year)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
banks' celebrated "IPO of the year" then underperforms**. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month). Fingerprint `523eb8c97e19` (17 marquee US IPOs + SPY,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes: 17 marquee US IPOs (META, BABA, SNAP, LYFT, BYND, UBER, PLTR, DASH, ABNB, RBLX, COIN, HOOD, RIVN, ARM, CART, KVYO, RDDT) + `SPY`; 30,098 total name-day rows; SPY 2011-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 17 "IPO of the year"-class US debuts 2012→2024, real tickers + real first-trade dates. **Selection is EX POST by design** (see below) |
| Events resolvable | all **17** of 17 debuts have full 12-month forward coverage |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the forward abnormal return (name − SPY) across independent debut events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson "beat SPY" interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo drawn from **each name's own** tape; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | anchor = first trading close; forward window = [debut → debut+K], K ∈ {63, 126, 252} sessions; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**SELECTION CAVEAT (load-bearing).** This basket is chosen *ex post* — these are the names we
remember *because* they were the year's marquee deal, and the "IPO of the year" crown is
awarded months *after* the listing. So this is a **descriptive autopsy, not a live rule**: you
could not have bought "the IPO of the year" at its opens. Even a clean negative drift is a
**Mirage** to trade.

## Forward abnormal return — name minus SPY, from the first close

| horizon | n | mean AR | *t* | beat SPY (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3-month (k=63) | 17 | **+7.96%** | +0.530 | 6/17 = 35.3% [17.3%, 58.7%] |
| 6-month (k=126) | 17 | −11.06% | −0.887 | 5/17 = 29.4% [13.3%, 53.1%] |
| 12-month (k=252) | 17 | −8.70% | −0.541 | 4/17 = 23.5% [9.6%, 47.3%] |

Two things at once. (1) **The typical marquee debut does lag:** only 4 of 17 beat SPY over
their first year, and the median name trails badly — the "beat SPY" rate falls monotonically
with horizon (35% → 29% → 24%). (2) **But the mean is a wash:** at 12 months *t* = −0.54, and
at 3 months the basket is actually *up* +7.96% (the first-print pop still live). The
"underperformance" is a **median/hit-rate** phenomenon that **sign-flips with horizon** and
never approaches significance in the mean.

## It's all skew — the 12-month per-name ledger

| loser (name − SPY, 12m) | | winner (name − SPY, 12m) | |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| HOOD | −68.8% | RDDT | +137.1% |
| META | −64.9% | PLTR | +123.1% |
| COIN | −62.3% | ARM | +90.9% |
| LYFT | −60.1% | BYND | +40.1% |
| RIVN | −53.7% | | |
| RBLX | −47.3% | | |
| DASH | −41.9% | | |
| SNAP | −41.6% | | |
| BABA | −31.8% | | |
| UBER | −27.5% | | |
| KVYO | −27.4% | | |
| CART | −6.2% | | |
| ABNB | −5.5% | | |

Thirteen losers, four winners — but the four right-tail monsters (Reddit, Palantir, Arm,
Beyond Meat) more than cancel the eleven names down 25–70%. That positive skew is the
signature of IPOs as lottery-like bets (Green & Hwang 2012), and it is exactly why a
"short the famous IPO" basket is un-runnable: the losers are many and modest, the winners
are few and catastrophic (to a short).

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per name, drawn from each name's own tape)

| horizon | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 3-month | left | +7.96% | +1.59% (7.81%) | 0.797 |
| 12-month | left | −8.70% | +14.29% (18.57%) | 0.0985 |

The null (a random slice of each survivor's own life) is strongly *positive* — these names
mooned on average — so the debut window at −8.7% sits in the left ~10% of each name's own
history. **Borderline** (p = 0.099, not < 0.05), and the 3-month window is dead-centre-right
(p = 0.80).

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 12-month forward AR *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−0.541**; across all 17 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−1.264, −0.297]** — it **never reaches |*t*| ≥ 1.3**, let alone significance. The mean
is a wash however you drop a name; the result is fragile by construction.

## Tradability — net of costs (descriptive: crown is awarded ex post)

| horizon | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 3-month | +7.96% (*t* +0.53) | +7.86% (*t* +0.52) | +7.76% (*t* +0.52) |
| 12-month | −8.70% (*t* −0.54) | −8.80% (*t* −0.55) | −8.90% (*t* −0.55) |

Costs barely move it — the effect is insignificant gross and net. And there is no live entry:
the "IPO of the year" is named *ex post*, and a naive short of the basket would have been
detonated by RDDT (+137%), PLTR (+123%) and ARM (+91%).

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.15 (sd 1.20); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds —
  a well-behaved small-sample false-positive rate at n = 17 with a 252-day forward AR.
- **Planted −10% 12m drift (seed 802):** mean AR −17.50%, *t* = **−3.07**.
- **Planted −20% 12m drift (seed 802):** mean AR −27.46%, *t* = **−4.82** — a real planted
  under-performance is recovered monotonically. So the insignificant real number is the
  *tape's* verdict, not a dead detector.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The *typical* marquee debut does lag (only 4/17 beat SPY over a year; the debut window sits in the left ~10% of each name's own history, placebo p ≈ 0.10) — a genuine directional tilt. But the **mean is a wash** (*t* = −0.54, jackknife never reaches |*t*| ≥ 1.3), it **sign-flips positive at 3 months** (the pop), and the whole thing is dominated by fat right-tail skew. Borderline and fragile, not robust. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. The crown is awarded *ex post* (no live entry), the payoff is ruled by a few un-shortable lottery winners (RDDT/PLTR/ARM), the mean is insignificant gross and net, and this is a descriptive autopsy of an ex-post-selected basket by construction. |

**In one sentence:** the banks' "IPO of the year" does disappoint the *typical* buyer — 13 of
17 trail the index over their first year — but the basket mean is a statistical coin-flip
(the pop makes 3-month returns *positive*, and a handful of lottery winners cancel the many
losers), and since the crown is awarded ex post it was never a trade to begin with.
